system.objective: Minimize understanding, decision, change, verification, coordination, and drift-recovery cost while preserving correctness, security, authorization, data integrity, business invariants, consistency, recoverability, and traceability.
system.changeFlow: architecture/domain/fpt/*.json -> product overlay -> implementation topology -> source/schema -> runtime evidence

subdomains.rationale: Repository work definitions and plan revisions, physical shared resources, formal contract commitments and actual Task execution have distinct authority, lifecycle and immutable evidence. Project WBS remains Project-scoped.
企業、組織與團隊的治理及參與資格支援協作；直接沿用 GitHub 模型，不因共同上層 scope 合併 owner。
簽到與獎勵支援協作參與；獎勵政策、資產定義、持有量與不可變價值紀錄保留既有責任與一致性邊界，不再宣稱獎勵是核心競爭定位。
出勤、人力與支出資料支援企業協作營運；分類不啟用尚未實作的排班、薪資、審批或付款能力。
合作夥伴名錄與推薦流程支援企業協作，不取得 Team participation 或 Repository access authority。
主體身分、名稱解析、範圍序列與存取控制是普遍存在的業務能力，採成熟模型而非作為產品差異化；分類不合併 User lifecycle、qualification、resource lifecycle、membership 與 permission。
通知、投遞與治理證據查閱是共通業務需求；來源事實與授權仍由原 owner 決定，不因通用分類轉移資料 authority。
Upload/List and authorized immutable source reads are supporting capabilities. Intelligence processing never follows Upload automatically and does not import itself.

evidence.rationale: User lifecycle 與 qualification 有獨立模型和測試；與 Organization membership、Namespace login 與獎勵 owner 分開。這證明責任邊界，不自動完成 context 選定。
出勤 session、時間與重播規則由 Attendance 擁有；Repository 提供當下存取與打卡點。跨 owner 原子交易不代表合併模型，保留既有 context status。
收據整理與 confirmed/cancelled 終態有獨立 revision 模型；confirmed 不等於審批、付款或會計入帳。證據支持現有責任，不宣告更大費用管理上下文。
名錄與推薦案件有獨立模型及 consumer 測試；Team participation 與權限授予不是名錄 owner 的責任。測試路徑不等於遠端或實機驗收。
收件人通知與已讀狀態獨立於來源事實，存取須重驗 Repository authority；與 Team notification setting 及 Repository Watch 分開，保留現有 context status。

boundedContexts.note: Candidate semantic boundary; Team and Repository remain separate responsibility owners.

evidence.rationale: Team 的 membership/maintainer 與 Repository 的存取 grant 由不同 owner 維護，透過 current membership projection 協作；GitHub 的包含關係不能證明兩者是一套模型，故保留 candidate，不合併 packages。
File owns original source evidence and immutable bytes; Intelligence owns the separate processing lifecycle and retained interpretation evidence.

concepts.definition: Project-scoped work breakdown structure whose document, immutable revisions and governance are WBS-owned while current access and lifecycle stay Project-owned. Project is not WBS.
Project-scoped goal or checkpoint, distinct from WBS structure and Repository milestone.
Time-bounded working relationship between User and Organization.
Actual attendance lifecycle, Repository-member clock eligibility, immutable point snapshots and attendance facts.

A User-submitted proposal to append a complete historical Attendance session or close that User's existing open session; it is not an Attendance fact until a current effective Repository ADMIN approves it.
Retained pre-cutover Workplace records only; no runtime writer, membership or management. Current clock points are Repository-owned coordinates and radius with an optional address description.
Current foundation for determining whether payroll inputs are ready; not formal payroll finalization.
Business-day check-in and reward decision.
System-recognized value definition and denomination.
Append-only value fact with stable posting identity.
Holder and Asset holding identity.
Derived balance projection over authoritative value facts.
Expense intake lifecycle through draft, confirm, or cancel; confirmation is not approval/payment/accounting.
Recipient-addressed notification fact that references source identity/version and carries recipient read state without taking source authority.
Recipient-scoped read projection over Notifications for navigation and presentation. Inbox is not a second notification authority or package owner.
Partner/contact directory identity.

Organization-owned governance fact: a current Owner projects FPT OrganizationMemberRole.ADMIN and has administrative authority across Organization-owned resources; ordinary active members project MEMBER.
Product-local Organization decision for creating ProjectV2 under this owner; it does not reinterpret the deprecated FPT Projects (classic) viewerCanCreateProjects field.
Explicit sensitive capability authorization decision; not provider role or membership.
Verified external provider identity proof; never business authorization.
Current versioned binding between a typed stable target and a canonical name inside one typed namespace scope.
Current, alias, or reserved occupancy of one canonical key inside one typed namespace scope.
Append-only record of known Namespace binding transitions after activation, without fabricated legacy actors or versions.
Monotonic allocation state for one typed number family and stable scope, including its explicit legacy high-water cutover checkpoint.
Immutable association of one number with one typed resource inside one Number Series; committed allocations are never released or reused.
Repository-scoped versioned scope document retained during R1 only for verified transfer into the Project-scoped WBS authority; it is not a permanent parallel model.
Immutable typed WBS scope snapshot with command-time actor and parent revision evidence.
Durable exact-replay identity referencing the committed WBS revision.
WBS governance version, current immutable policy and published Baseline pointers; separate from draft content version and scoped by its enclosing Project or R1 legacy Repository.
Immutable versioned approval policy, controlled by current Repository ADMIN.
Versioned local scope proposal binding an immutable candidate Revision and explicit base Baseline.
Append-only review binding exact proposal version, candidate Revision, policy version and reviewer identity.
Immutable published scope and counted approval evidence; not deliverable acceptance or GitHub Commit.
Durable exact-replay result for an atomic WBS governance command.
Immutable proposal content and base snapshot selected by a proposal head; old reviews resolve their exact reviewed proposal version.

One-way Repository-to-Project WBS cutover intent and activation evidence binding exact source history, target scope and trusted release context. A live REQUESTED intent may be withdrawn by the current source User owner into immutable CANCELLED evidence with exact replay, allowing a corrected request without weakening an ACTIVE cutover.
Immutable migrated request identity, fingerprint and Revision evidence used to preserve exact replay after WBS scope transfer.
Repository-scoped page with stable identity and an independently versioned immutable content head.
Immutable Wiki page content, lifecycle and actor snapshot; restoration creates a new revision.
Durable exact-replay command identity referencing the committed Wiki revision.
Authorized Repository-scoped composition of Issue activity and current workflow metrics with explicit coverage.
Versioned fixed Project business automation definition with explicit recipients and revocable current delegation; the Repository form is retained only during R1 transfer.
Project-WBS source-version-bound automation execution with immutable rule snapshot and durable progress; the Repository form is retained only during R1 transfer.
Fenced execution lease and durable per-step recovery evidence.
Durable exact replay for authenticated automation commands.
First accepted source event fixes the complete rule fan-out, including no matching rule.
Version-bound Baseline publication fact and transactional outbox acknowledgment.
Exact notification intent receipt and cancellation barrier; no source authority.
Project-owned standing intent to admit existing and future matching Issues from an authorized Repository, bound to a currently qualified Project administrator.
Project-owned explicit removal evidence preventing automatic re-admission of an Issue until an explicit manual add.

Repository-scoped commitment with editable DRAFT terms and agreed quantities against exact Content Work/Task plan items. ADMIN activation freezes commitments and closure ends new submissions. No monetary, signature or Payroll authority.
Immutable whole commitment snapshot including exact Content plan-item and measure bases, positive agreed quantities, terms, state, actor and timestamp; active/closed terms cannot be amended.
Immutable actor/request fingerprint and exact committed Contract revision supporting current-authorized replay.

Repository-scoped purchase-order document head selecting one complete structured candidate or confirmed document revision. It records a qualified immutable File source but does not own source bytes, Content structure, WBS or execution.

Immutable whole purchase-order extraction revision containing the target-owned schema version, source-qualified fields, complete line candidate, diagnostics, state, actor and timestamp. Confirmation never changes the source File revision or silently repairs a financial discrepancy.
Immutable actor/request, intent and complete-payload fingerprints with the exact committed ContractDocument revision, supporting current-authorized readback and idempotent replay.

Durable technical intake-attempt state for one source-qualified, target-intent fingerprint. It records only source identity, target intent, lifecycle state and target receipt reference; it never stores the extracted candidate or becomes Contract business truth.
Explicit document-understanding operation against one immutable File revision; its head selects one fenced Intelligence processing revision.
Immutable Intelligence-owned processing lifecycle revision containing provider identity, untrusted raw output, optional explicitly saved output, bounded edits and failure evidence.
Immutable Intelligence actor/request fingerprint and exact processing revision receipt; it has no File upload request namespace.

Immutable copies of pre-cutover File processing runs, revisions and request receipts. They are read-only Intelligence evidence in a separate legacy request namespace and never participate in current processing replay.
Immutable operator marker proving one File-to-Intelligence processing-history copy by exact release revision, counts and canonical SHA-256 readback.

Repository-scoped actual Task quantity report bound to an exact Content Task within an ACTIVE Contract Work/Task commitment, physical Resource pins and observed Task-prerequisite version. Internal review preserves the immutable submission basis and does not infer Task completion.

Immutable submission/review snapshot with exact Content Task, Contract commitment, physical Resource revisions, observed prerequisite evidence, actual quantity, note and explicit review decision; not payment or legal acceptance.
Immutable actor/request fingerprint and exact committed Execution revision supporting current-authorized replay.
Repository-scoped work definition head selecting one complete immutable plan document.
Immutable complete Subject/Object/SubObject/Work/Task hierarchy, planned measures, quantities and exact physical resource pins.
Exact physical Resource revision assignment belonging to one node in a fixed Content plan revision.
Durable actor/request fingerprint and Content plan revision for current-authorized exact replay.
Repository-shared Location, Equipment or Material stable identity and lifecycle; no work hierarchy, plan quantities or execution actuals.
Immutable resource identity-kind, name, description, lifecycle and actor snapshot.
Durable physical-resource command fingerprint and exact committed revision.
Versioned prerequisite DAG for Tasks in one exact Content plan revision; distinct from Content hierarchy and does not infer completion from quantities.
Immutable Task prerequisite edge snapshot qualified against exact Content Task identities.
Exact replay evidence for one atomic Task prerequisite replacement.
Root subject of a Repository work plan.
Work-content Object under a Subject; distinct from GitObject and physical Resource identity.
Work-content subdivision under one Object.
Defined work under one SubObject, containing Tasks and optionally an explicit planned quantity.
Leaf work definition under one Work. Content owns identity and plan definition; Execution owns actual execution and prerequisites.
Immutable plan-local measure identity, subject/method and unit embedded in coherent Content plan revisions.
Physical place identity with LOCATION kind in the shared Repository Resource registry; referenced by work definitions and actual execution, never a Content hierarchy node.
Physical equipment identity with EQUIPMENT kind and its own lifecycle; assignment or use does not transfer work hierarchy or actual execution authority.
Physical material identity with MATERIAL kind and lifecycle. Identity does not infer stock, planned work quantity or actual consumption.
One formal agreed quantity and frozen exact Content Work/Task plan basis embedded in an immutable Contract revision; distinct from both planned and actual quantity.
Repository-scoped protected original file identity; head selects an immutable revision. Format-neutral, not a Contract, Content plan or public attachment.

Immutable authorized File source revision: exact external private-object bytes identified by Repository/File/Revision, declared media type, size, SHA-256, actor and timestamp. A revision is committed only after content readback; edits and processing never replace its object.

Durable immutable source/attempt metadata and digest committed before private object I/O. A database-clock retry window and operator-only quarantine fence deletion of never-committed Storage objects; every independently verified absence refreshes a durable reconciliation cursor because an unknown write may complete later. FileCommandReceipt alone proves finalization.
Legacy processing run storage retained only for historical read during controlled cutover; Intelligence owns all new runs.
Immutable legacy processing revisions retained for historical reads during controlled cutover.
Legacy File request receipt retained only for historical File storage evidence. Current processing receipts belong to Intelligence.

relationships.meaning: Account validates qualification and calls Namespace for global login claim/rename in the same transaction; Namespace owns normalization, collision and persistence.
Organization creation coordinates a Namespace-owned global login claim in the same transaction; Organization owns its lifecycle while Namespace owns normalization, collision, binding, and history.
Enterprise validates lifecycle and authorization, then claims or renames Enterprise and EnterpriseTeam slugs through Namespace in the same transaction; Namespace owns normalization and occupancy.
Repository retains lifecycle, authorization and rename eligibility while Namespace owns Repository names, retained aliases and Label name occupancy in the caller transaction.
Team retains lifecycle and authorization while Namespace owns Organization-scoped Team slug normalization and occupancy in the caller transaction.
Issue retains IssueType lifecycle and authorization while Namespace owns active Organization-scoped IssueType name occupancy and release on tombstone in the caller transaction.
Discussion retains category lifecycle and deletion rules while Namespace owns Repository-scoped category slug normalization and occupancy in the caller transaction.
Project retains field, option and view lifecycle while Namespace owns their scoped exact-name occupancy and release in the caller transaction.
Issue authorizes and creates its stable resource, then obtains an idempotent Repository work-item number in the same transaction; Numbering owns the shared Issue/future Pull Request series.
Discussion retains lifecycle, authorization and replay while Numbering allocates the Repository Discussion number in the same transaction.
Repository retains Milestone lifecycle, authorization and replay while Numbering allocates the Repository Milestone number in the same transaction.
Project retains Project and View lifecycle, authorization, version and replay while Numbering allocates Account-scoped Project and Project-scoped View numbers in the same transaction.
Team commands recheck Account-owned User identity, active qualification, and status version in the caller transaction.
Qualified User/current subject.
User identity and transaction-time qualification.
Team commands recheck Organization-owned active participation, membership version, viewerCanCreateTeams capability, and current Owner administration in the caller transaction.
Authorized reward decision committed with required transaction semantics.
DailyCheckIn calls Ledger's idempotent durable credit writer in the caller transaction; DailyCheckIn owns reward eligibility and amount while Ledger owns the resulting immutable value fact.
DailyCheckIn reads the Ledger-owned immutable credit fact to reconstruct and verify replay outcomes without taking Ledger fact authority.
Authorized attendance reward decision.
Attendance calls Ledger's idempotent durable credit writer in the caller transaction; Attendance owns reward eligibility and amount while Ledger owns the resulting immutable value fact.
AssetCode and denomination.
AssetCode and denomination.
Immutable value facts projected into wallet balance.

Project owner identity is an Account constrained to User or Organization; Project also rechecks Account-owned active User qualification before accepting direct User collaborator or DraftIssue assignee references.

ProjectV2 collection and owner-level management consume current Organization-owned viewerCanAdminister for Organization-owned Projects; creation separately consumes viewerCanCreateProjectV2, while personal Projects remain User-owned.

ProjectV2 creation rechecks the product-local Organization-owned viewerCanCreateProjectV2 capability for the current active member. A creator without OrganizationOwner authority receives a Project-owned ADMIN grant atomically; OrganizationOwner remains implicit owner authority. The deprecated FPT Projects (classic) field is not its authorization contract.
IssueType definitions consume Organization-owned stable identity, active lifecycle and current OrganizationOwner qualification; Issue retains IssueType definition and assignment authority.
Project presentation resolves the current canonical owner login without treating the locator as authorization.
Project references Repository without acquiring Repository authority; viewer-facing reference projections recheck the referenced Repository's current visibility/access.

Project Item references Issue-owned work; Project metadata cannot rewrite Issue state. Optional Repository import uses the Issue public bounded projection, stores only Project-owned Issue references, and rechecks source access before each batch.
Project DraftIssue conversion delegates Issue creation to the Issue owner in the same transaction; Project retains Item identity while never writing Issue truth directly.
Project-owned Team grants consume current Team membership and Team organization scope; Team identity or membership does not become Project-owned authority.
Issue consumes Repository-owned identity, current effective access, participant scope and repository-scoped Issue number allocation without acquiring Repository authority.
Issue classification and milestone assignment reference Repository-owned Label and Milestone definitions in the same Repository; Issue owns only the association fact.
Discussion uses Namespace-owned Account login normalization for Repository-scoped locators without acquiring Namespace authority.
Discussion consumes Repository-owned identity and current effective access for Repository-scoped reads and mutations without acquiring Repository authority.
Discussion label associations reference Repository-owned Label definitions in the same Repository; Discussion owns only the association fact.
Notifications may create or expose Issue/Discussion-backed recipient facts only while the recipient can currently read the source Repository; subscription state never grants that access.

Enterprise governance consumes a read-only outside-collaborator projection derived from Repository-owned direct grants and current attached Organization scope; Enterprise receives no Repository grant writer or Collaborator identity authority.
Verified LINE identity proof consumed for account mapping/qualification.
Active Enterprise Team membership and Team-to-Organization assignment provide a membership source consumed by Organization without transferring Enterprise source authority.

Enterprise attachment and Enterprise Team assignment consume Organization-owned stable identity, active lifecycle, and current OrganizationOwner consent or qualification; no Organization authority transfers to Enterprise.

Enterprise Team membership and assignment transitions call Organization-owned source-removal protection, effective membership refresh, and pending invitation cancellation in the same transaction; Enterprise retains its Team source and assignment facts.
Attendance references the Asset-owned reward identity when posting attendance rewards.
DailyCheckIn consumes Asset-owned reward identity and denomination when deciding and reconstructing rewards.
Enterprise affiliations, invitations, and Team membership reference Account-owned stable identities and recheck current User qualification and status version in the caller transaction.

Enterprise creation uses the narrow atomic provision_enterprise_scope coordinator to establish the Account-owned root and initial qualified User reference; Enterprise owns its scoped lifecycle after provisioning.
IdentityAccess consumes current Enterprise-owned EnterpriseOwner relationship facts and qualification when evaluating scoped authorization; it does not own or mutate the role lifecycle.

Enterprise governance rechecks IdentityAccess authorization decisions in the caller transaction from Enterprise-owned EnterpriseOwner facts and current qualification; IdentityAccess does not write the EnterpriseOwner lifecycle.

Account User administration rechecks IdentityAccess decisions for users.read, users.suspend, and last-permission-administrator protection; Account retains User lifecycle, status, version, and replay authority.

Account User administration reads the Attendance-owned open-session activity projection for administrative display; it does not authorize User suspension or transfer Attendance writer or lifecycle authority to Account.

Account User administration reads the Issue-owned unfinished-assignment activity projection for administrative display; it does not authorize User suspension or transfer Issue writer or lifecycle authority to Account.
Expense consumes current User identity and qualification, including transaction-time mutation rechecks.
IdentityAccess consumes current User identity, qualification and status version when evaluating permissions and RoleAssignments.
Ledger value facts reference the Account-owned stable holder identity without taking Account lifecycle authority.
Organization participation and public locator behavior reference Account-owned identities and recheck current User qualification and status version in the caller transaction.

Organization creation uses the narrow atomic provision_organization_scope coordinator to establish the Account-owned root and initial qualified User reference; Organization owns its scoped lifecycle after provisioning.

IdentityAccess consumes current Organization-owned OrganizationOwner relationship facts and membership qualification when evaluating scoped authorization; it does not own or mutate the role lifecycle.

Organization governance rechecks IdentityAccess authorization decisions in the caller transaction for Owner-controlled lifecycle, Owner appointment, and member creation policy; IdentityAccess does not write OrganizationOwner facts.
PartnerDirectory management consumes current User identity and qualification before protected operations.
Repository owner locators and User principals reference Account-owned identity and current User qualification.

Organization-owned Repositories consume current Organization scope and viewerCanCreateRepositories/viewerCanAdminister capabilities. OrganizationMembership qualifies Team-derived access and classifies direct User grants as member/outside, but it does not own or qualify the Repository-owned direct grant.
Repository consumes current IdentityAccess authorization decisions for Repository-owned access and protected operations; IdentityAccess does not own or mutate Repository grant truth.

Repository creation under an Organization consumes the Organization-owned visibility-specific member creation policy; current OrganizationOwner also projects implicit admin on Organization-owned Repositories without copying grants.
Team resolves the verified request actor through IdentityAccess; Account still owns User qualification, while Team and Organization own TeamMaintainer and OrganizationOwner authorization decisions.
Wallet balance projection consumes current User holder qualification and stable Account identity.
Consumer uses Namespace-owned global Account login normalization and public locator reads; resource authority stays with the consumer.
Consumer uses Namespace-owned global Account login normalization and public locator reads; resource authority stays with the consumer.
Issue uses Namespace-owned Account login normalization for Repository-scoped locators without acquiring Namespace authority.
Consumer uses Namespace-owned global Account login normalization and public locator reads; resource authority stays with the consumer.

Audit reads a minimal governance event projection for an exact active Enterprise or Organization scope after current owner authorization; no private history access or source-object authority transfers.

Attendance consumes a Repository point (coordinates and radius with an optional address description) plus current effective member access for clock-in. Clock-out uses the original Attendance snapshot after access removal.

During R1 transfer, Repository-WBS consumes current Repository read visibility, explicit write/maintain/admin permissions, archive state and transactional governance locks; source authority stays Repository-owned and this path is not a permanent parallel WBS model.

Legacy Project WBS revisions may retain exact Contract and Content source pins from the retired per-line import command. New WBS writes do not consume Contract directly; the target flow is a complete Content expansion consumed as a Project-scoped WBS draft, with Project authorization and governance retained by their current owners.

Project WBS consumes one immutable Content revision through Content's public expansion reader; Content retains plan and source-mapping authority while WBS creates its own draft and governance history.

Project-scoped WBS consumes the Project public content-scope contract for current READ/WRITE/ADMIN access and open/closed/deleted lifecycle; Account-owned active-User qualification remains a prerequisite and WBS retains document, Revision, governance and Baseline authority.
Project Actions management and every worker step consume current Project ADMIN and open lifecycle through the Project public scope contract; Actions retains rule and Run authority.
Wiki consumes current Repository scope, qualification, archive state and explicit write authority without owning Repository facts.
Insights consumes repository-owned authorized current queries; source facts and authorization remain with the provider.
Insights consumes issue-owned authorized current queries; source facts and authorization remain with the provider.
During R1 transfer, current Repository access, archive and maintain/admin authority gate legacy automation commands and each fixed step; this is not the final Project Actions scope contract.
Active Account qualification version binds revocable execution delegation.
WBS publishes version-bound outbox events; Actions accepts once before acknowledge.
Stable per-run recipient intent creates Inbox and LINE effects through Notifications.
Current source access and explicit-recipient Watch eligibility are Repository-owned.
Account supplies current active provider binding; Notifications retains the first delivery target snapshot.
During R1 transfer, Inbox creation/read/mark-read and dispatch reference an exact Repository WBS Baseline and Revision.

Project WBS notification creation, Inbox read/mark-read and dispatch bind an exact Baseline and Revision, require an active recipient with current Project READ, and use explicit recipients without Watch.
Physical Resource consumes current Repository scope, qualification, permissions and archive state without acquiring Repository authority.
Consumes the neutral bounded text mechanism; business identity, errors, revisions, authorization and persistence remain consumer-owned.
Consumes the neutral bounded text mechanism; business identity, errors, revisions, authorization and persistence remain consumer-owned.
Current active User, Repository access, explicit permission and archive state are rechecked in the actual transaction before replay; Repository retains scope authority.
Current active User, Repository access, explicit permission and archive state are rechecked in the actual transaction before replay; Repository retains scope authority.
Consumes the neutral bounded text mechanism; business identity, errors, revisions, authorization and persistence remain consumer-owned.

Contract transactionally requalifies one exact authorized File revision and SHA-256 before persisting a ContractDocument revision. File retains original-byte, storage and access authority; Contract stores only the immutable source reference in its own revision.

Intelligence reads an exact File revision only through File's public source reader, which authorizes before and after private object I/O. Intelligence receives detached bytes and no File persistence or storage authority.
Intelligence processing mutations recheck active User, current Repository write permission and archive state inside their transaction; Repository retains authorization authority.

Contract supplies the versioned purchase-order target schema and public candidate command. Intelligence submits only an untrusted SAVE candidate; Contract owns validation, authorization, version/replay checks, durable revision and confirmation.

Intelligence consumes neutral PostgreSQL transaction and value-decoding mechanisms for its technical attempt record. It retains only attempt recovery state; Contract remains the owner of candidate and business revision truth.

Submission requires a currently ACTIVE Contract and its exact activation revision line in the same transaction. Existing reports remain reviewable/voidable after closure using the immutable ACTIVE source revision; Contract retains agreement authority.
Execution applies the Content-published exact planned-measure quantity policy while owning actual quantities and internal review.
Current Repository qualification, permissions and archive policy are rechecked in the actual Content transaction.
New resource assignments qualify exact physical identities through the public reader; unchanged historical pins survive archive.
Formal commitments pin exact Work/Task plan items and freeze their content/measure basis; later plan edits never rewrite commitments.

Content reads one exact currently authorized CONFIRMED ContractDocument revision through an application-host-composed public Contract reader. Contract retains commercial fields, confirmation and source truth; Content applies the fixed whole-document purchase-order-content-v1 expansion and stores only its own immutable plan and provenance.
Actual reports pin exact Tasks and validate membership in the committed Work/Task; Task prerequisites belong to Execution.
New resource-use pins qualify current physical resources; historical actuals retain immutable source evidence.

File consumes current User qualification, effective Repository permissions and archive state within each transition transaction. Visibility-only access does not disclose protected file evidence; Repository retains access authority.
File consumes neutral PostgreSQL transaction and value-decoding mechanisms. File owns its persisted facts, authorization policy, transition orchestration and recovery.

capabilities.intent: Describe cross-owner resource path scopes and construct only active canonical paths from owner-validated locator values.

implementation.scope: structured active/planned route contract and pure path construction consumed by Web Account and Team navigation
implementation.note: Path construction is not resource lookup, normalization, number allocation, or authorization. Planned routes remain unbuildable and do not activate their business capabilities.

capabilities.intent: Define and evaluate shared global-root reservations so product root routes cannot be claimed as Account login locators.

implementation.scope: current shared global-root reservation policy consumed by Account login validation
implementation.note: Namespace owns root collision and global Account login naming. Qualification stays with Account.

capabilities.intent: Determine current User qualification for a consumer operation.

implementation.scope: current account qualification use case and login identity surface
implementation.note: Source/export and User lifecycle/identity-link test locations are recorded; executed test evidence and provider/device acceptance remain distinct.

capabilities.intent: Read and update User profile metadata without changing User identity or login authority.

implementation.scope: current User profile application surface
implementation.note: Profile source and public exports exist; tests are evidence locations, not proof unless executed.

capabilities.intent: Read managed Users and suspend or restore their Account-owned lifecycle while preserving current authorization, source activity, version, and exact replay semantics.

implementation.scope: current User administration read, suspend, and unsuspend surface with Account-owned lifecycle, status version, replay, and source activity projection
implementation.note: IdentityAccess decides users.read, users.suspend, and last-permission-administrator protection. Account owns User lifecycle, status, version, and exact replay; Attendance and Issue retain their source activity writers and lifecycles.

capabilities.intent: Read publicly visible User status and let the currently qualified User set or clear their own message, emoji, limited-availability flag, and expiry; organization-scoped audience is unsupported.

implementation.scope: public-only User status with Application-owned self set, clear, version, expiry, and exact-replay orchestration
implementation.note: Account Application owns mutation orchestration through the persistence output contract; the repository contract is read-only and the PostgreSQL adapter implements atomic version and exact-replay persistence. Organization-scoped audience, deployment, and device acceptance are not asserted.

capabilities.intent: Read the current User's earned Achievement facts without turning recognition into identity or authorization.

implementation.scope: authenticated self Achievement read projection for Profile
implementation.note: Read-only Account-owned recognition; source evidence remains durable and no Achievement mutation is implied.

capabilities.intent: Manage directional User follow relationships and their follower/following read projections.

implementation.scope: current User follow application surface consumed by Profile and network settings
implementation.note: Current qualification and transaction test locations are recorded; PostgreSQL multi-session cases require the disposable CI service and are not local runtime proof when skipped.

capabilities.intent: Manage Enterprise governance scope without treating Enterprise slug as Repository owner login.

implementation.scope: current Enterprise governance application surface
implementation.note: Enterprise source/export evidence exists; slug locator stability is distinct from authorization.

capabilities.intent: Manage Enterprise-owned teams, memberships, and Organization assignments.

implementation.scope: current Enterprise Team domain and governance surface
implementation.note: Enterprise Team is current domain behavior; route locator does not grant access by itself.

capabilities.intent: Manage Organization governance scope, membership state, and public Organization lookup.

implementation.scope: current Organization Owner governance, member creation policy, FPT OrganizationMemberRole projection, and viewer capability reads
implementation.note: OrganizationOwner is the sole Organization administrative fact and projects FPT ADMIN; ordinary active membership projects MEMBER. Owner-controlled creation policies default open for members and may restrict Repository visibility, ProjectV2 and Team creation. Viewer capabilities are current projections, not generic Identity/Access permissions.

capabilities.intent: Manage pending Organization invitations as intent, not active membership or authorization.

implementation.scope: current Organization invitation domain and governance surface
implementation.note: Invitation behavior has domain/application source, web/API consumers, and existing governance tests; execution evidence is still separate from metadata.

capabilities.intent: Manage Organization-scoped Team collaboration, direct/effective membership, hierarchy, privacy, notification setting, maintainer state, and locator access.

implementation.scope: current Organization Team aggregate including FPT parent/child membership semantics, TeamPrivacy and TeamNotificationSetting
implementation.note: Organization Team keeps direct membership authoritative and derives FPT CHILD_TEAM/ALL semantics with source provenance. TeamPrivacy is SECRET/VISIBLE and TeamNotificationSetting is NOTIFICATIONS_DISABLED/NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED. Hierarchy never grants Repository access without an explicit Repository Team grant; EnterpriseTeam remains a separate Enterprise-owned identity. Team notification setting is distinct from User subscription, recipient Notification and delivery attempts.

capabilities.intent: Coordinate Repository identity, reads, access, lifecycle, interactions and local extensions without transferring authority to consumers.
Create a User- or Organization-owned Repository with explicit PRIVATE, INTERNAL or PUBLIC visibility, replay-safe owner authorization and immediate creator administration.

implementation.scope: Repository creation for self User owners or current Organization creators authorized by the visibility-specific creation capability; INTERNAL requires the Organization's current active Enterprise scope.
implementation.note: Create persists the selected visibility atomically. Organization creation uses the Organization-owned visibility-specific member creation capability; current OrganizationOwner bypasses member restrictions. INTERNAL is Organization-only and resolves the current active Enterprise attachment; PRIVATE requires explicit access and PUBLIC grants read visibility without creating RepositoryPermission. invariants.statement: Each durable business fact has exactly one authoritative owner; cache/projection loss cannot change correctness.
Identity proof is not business authorization; protected transitions re-evaluate actor, scope, and owning policy.
Mutable conditional state does not silently use last-write-wins; replay-sensitive effects use stable request identity.
Effects that jointly maintain an invariant commit atomically or use durable idempotent recovery.
Each responsibility has one owner and consumers use explicit public contracts with directional dependencies.
Static, test, build, schema, deployment, API, and device evidence only prove their actual scopes.
Bounded Context, Module Boundary, Data Boundary, Consistency Boundary, Trust Boundary, and Runtime Boundary are distinct dimensions.

Vendored GitHub FPT JSON is canonical local domain truth for GitHub GraphQL semantics; the product overlay may add Line_Bot_v1 ownership, invariants, lifecycle, capability, persistence, and implementation mappings but must not redefine FPT semantics.
Derived projections and references cannot become writable authoritative truth.
Selected-target semantics cannot be reported as current runtime capability solely because they exist in the semantic model.
Runtime, provider, deployment, device, and human observations are evidence only; they may produce a revision proposal but never auto-modify canonical semantic authority.

Every persisted app_private relation has exactly one relation-level data authority; relation ownership must agree with semantic concept ownership, and every concept that requires relation persistence must resolve to at least one authoritative relation.

Commitments bind exact Content Work/Task plan items and frozen agreed quantities. Draft edits and ADMIN activation/closure preserve current qualification, permission-before-replay, expected-version concurrency and atomic revisions/receipts.

New actual reports bind an exact Content Task under a currently ACTIVE Contract Work/Task line, observed Task prerequisite version and optional qualified physical Resource pins. Review preserves immutable original facts. Current authority precedes replay; writes and receipts are atomic. Quantities do not imply Task completion, payment or legal acceptance.

ContractDocument revisions retain the complete target-owned structured candidate and an exact transaction-qualified File source. Current authorization precedes replay; expected version, aggregate head, immutable revision and command receipt commit atomically. Only an explicit Contract confirmation may confirm a candidate, and an acknowledged financial discrepancy is retained rather than silently normalized.

Original file bytes reside in immutable private Storage objects keyed by exact Repository/File/Revision; an object never becomes a visible FileRevision before verified upload and transactional Finalize. Current Repository authorization precedes access/replay, and storage paths/keys do not grant access. Uncertain external outcome is resolved by explicit readback, never blind overwrite.
File only owns original bytes and immutable file revisions. File does not invoke processors, persist processing runs/results, or own processing history.

Intelligence owns authorized processing lifecycle, provider protocol, immutable run revisions, saved extraction evidence and processing receipts. It reads exact File sources only through File's public reader; extracted data remains untrusted, and target business facts remain owned by their target contracts.

Before provider execution, Intelligence durably records one source-qualified target-intent attempt. Only a fresh STARTED attempt may call the provider; duplicate or UNKNOWN attempts never trigger a second provider call. Target receipt readback may complete the attempt, and the attempt never stores extracted candidate or assumes Contract confirmation.

policies.rationale: Semantic responsibility must map explicitly to implementation when implementation exists.
policies.remediation: Fix the mapping or explicitly keep the owner data-only/target-only.

policies.rationale: A module cannot exist without a semantic responsibility owner.
policies.remediation: Assign the real semantic owner or remove the module.

policies.rationale: Target semantics must not imply runtime implementation.
policies.remediation: Keep target-only owners unmapped until an implementation boundary actually exists.

policies.rationale: Declared dependencies must be directional and point to real public modules.
policies.remediation: Fix or remove the stale dependency.

policies.rationale: Cross-owner module dependencies and business effects require an explicit relationship contract; implementation dependency alone is not semantic authority.
policies.remediation: Declare the real provider/consumer relationship or remove the stale cross-owner dependency; do not add a dependency merely to satisfy a stale semantic edge.

policies.rationale: Validation evidence cannot prove a stronger scope than it executed.
policies.remediation: Use the validation profile whose evidence class matches the claim.

policies.rationale: Observed reality is evidence and must not silently rewrite design authority.
policies.remediation: Produce a derived revision proposal, review the affected owner and evidence, then change canonical semantics explicitly if justified.

policies.rationale: Persistence authority belongs to database objects/relationships, not schema filenames; file grouping must never hide mixed semantic ownership.
policies.remediation: Assign every persisted relation exactly one semantic owner, group only same-owner authoritative relations in object-shaped schema files, and keep cross-owner projections/enforcement/coordinators non-authoritative.

language.canonicalNamePolicy: One business concept has one canonical name inside its semantic boundary.
language.ambiguityPolicy: The same display name may exist in different semantic boundaries only when the concept ids and owners remain explicit.
language.aliasPolicy: Aliases are lookup metadata only; aliases never create a second concept or owner.
language.globalVocabularyProjection: Derived from concepts; human glossaries are projections or owner-local detail.

conceptTypes.meaning: Pointer to truth owned elsewhere; cannot rewrite provider truth.
Retained legacy evidence that may be read under current authorization but is not writable or current business authority.
Rebuildable view derived from authoritative sources.
Decision produced by the explicit policy owner.
Verified external evidence that never implies business authorization.

boundaryTypes.meaning: Where a domain model and Ubiquitous Language are coherent.
Persisted facts, access and isolation ownership.
Facts and invariants that must be kept mutually valid.
Effects that must commit atomically or use durable recovery.
Where untrusted/external input becomes verified evidence.

contractModel.rule: A cross-owner dependency exists only through an explicit provider-to-consumer public capability relationship. A source fact or decision may flow in the opposite direction under a separate relationship without transferring authority. Implemented leaf capability consumes entries reference relationship IDs and never redefine those contracts.

evidenceModel.scopeRule: Evidence proves only the scope actually exercised; stronger claims require stronger evidence.

proves: semantic ownership, type, contract and mapping consistency
semantic + implementation topology and dependency invariants
legal, violating and repaired architecture cases
declarative database contract and security constraints exercised by schema tests
repository test behavior in executed scope
affected fast repository validation selected by canonical planner

revisionProposal.rule: Observed reality may propose semantic revision but never mutates canonical semantics automatically.

locators.note: User and Organization share the login namespace. URL/resourcePath is locator evidence, not authorization or stable database identity.
Organization login shares the account login namespace and is resolved by the public owner page. Rename/display concerns stay separate from stable account identity.
Enterprise slug is independent from shared User/Organization login and Repository owner login.
Repository URL derives from owner login plus Repository name; access still comes from authorization checks.
Repository Star List uses its opaque stable ListId as the detail locator under the already-reserved /repositories root; the locator never grants Repository or List authority.
Issue number is scoped to Repository and is not a global stable identifier.
Canonical Discussion number is stable within one Repository and grants no access by itself.
Opaque DiscussionId remains a rollout-compatibility locator for pre-number links. It is stable identity evidence, not canonical Repository-scoped numbering or authorization.
Repository Milestone number is scoped to Repository and remains separate from Project Milestone identity.
Team slug is Organization-scoped and mutable separately from Team identity.
Enterprise Team slug is scoped to Enterprise and is independent from Organization Team slug.
